fluff.overview: The Machina Domini Interface Armor was a prototype light power armor suit developed by the Word of Blake during the final years of the Jihad. Part of the secretive Machina Domini program, the suit served a role unlike any other battle armor design. Rather than functioning as an independent infantry system, the armor acted as a neural bridge between its wearer and a specially equipped BattleMech, allowing a single cybernetically augmented trooper to control both simultaneously. The experimental technology required specialized neural implants and saw only limited production.
fluff.capabilities:
Weighing 400 kilograms, the Machina Domini Interface Armor was one of the heavier light power armor designs of its era. Its primary function was not independent combat but serving as the control layer between a VDNI-equipped warrior and a modified BattleMech cockpit. Bio-feedback and neural-impulse systems within the suit eliminated the need for a conventional gyro and most diagnostic computer functions in the host machine, saving considerable tonnage and internal space.

For self-defense, the suit mounted a Firedrake Support Needler in the right arm and an anti-personnel weapon mount in the left, with armored gloves on both hands. Standard armor provided substantial protection for the suit's weight class. Ground speed was modest, and the armor lacked any jump capability. The absolute dependence on VDNI implants restricted its use to cyborg Manei Domini operatives, a limitation that proved both a security feature and a fatal bottleneck for wider adoption.
fluff.deployment: Each Machina Domini Interface Armor suit was paired with a specific BattleMech fitted with a compatible interface cockpit, with the trooper serving simultaneously as the machine's pilot. Field testing on Gibson saw the suits deployed alongside Gestalt prototypes in combat roles ranging from ambush operations to high-speed pursuit, providing valuable operational data during the program's brief existence.
fluff.history:
The Machina Domini program was the work of Doctor Devon Cortland, known within the Word of Blake as Precentor Vapula. The program aimed to merge trooper and BattleMech into a unified fighting system, using a specialized power armor suit as the control interface between a cybernetically augmented warrior and a modified cockpit. Gibson Federated BattleMechs on Gibson served as the production site for the prototype suits and their companion BattleMech, the Gestalt.

Only a small number of prototypes reached completion before Regulan forces destroyed Gibson in 3078, eliminating the production facilities and most of the program's technical infrastructure. A handful of suits and roughly a dozen Gestalts were evacuated ahead of the planet's fall. The Republic of the Sphere subsequently made concerted efforts to track down and destroy the surviving prototypes, viewing the technology as too dangerous to persist. With the disappearance of the remaining Manei Domini and the collapse of their military organization, the original interface armor was classified as obsolete by 3081. Rumors persisted that the underlying technology had not been entirely eradicated.
